new_statements.quote: In general the lower of the above vocoid phones is to be understood. Stress is marked only if it falls on other than the first syllable not containing [a]. Stress does not appear to be a phonemic feature in any of these languages. The entire question of the phonemic interpretation of suspicious vocoid sequences is very complex and no consistency should be ex- pected in the transcription.

new_statements.relation_note: Stress non-phonemic in all languages surveyed; default stress position = first non-schwa syllable (transcription convention); Wapei-Palei phylum phonology: three positions of articulation, no voiced/voiceless contrast, five to eight vowels; nothing on tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Fieldworker's survey-level statement: in none of the Lumi Subdistrict languages he recorded (Wiaki among them) does stress appear to be phonemic; his transcription leaves stress unmarked when it falls on the first syllable whose vowel is not schwa (the default case) and writes it only when it falls elsewhere. In the published 42-item Wiaki list 41 items are unmarked (= stress on the first full-vowel syllable) and one, lahə́ 'arm', is marked (stress on a schwa-vowel second syllable). Net reading for Wiaki: non-contrastive stress, by default on the leftmost non-schwa syllable (quality-sensitive, near-initial).
new_statements.exceptions: Only via marking: Wiaki lahə́ 'arm' carries stress on a schwa syllable contrary to the default; Laycock adds that 'no consistency should be expected in the transcription' of vocoid sequences and that excrescent (epenthetic) vowels are strongly reduced in stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Wiaki (Menandon, Minendon, Wiakei), pop. 530, villages Binara, Surimorta, Walgon, Wemil = ISO wii Minidien (renamed 2007); this is Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for mini1253 and the source of the transnewguinea/Rosetta lists. The stress sentences are a blanket statement over all the Lumi Subdistrict wordlists in the article (Torricelli/Wapei-Palei plus a few Sepik languages), Wiaki included; 'Menandon/Minendon' is also an alt name of Yangum (Aiku) -- not confused here since the entry names Walgon/Wemil.
